pageCache.pageTitle: Melbury College - Welcome from the Head of School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
Canterbury Campus is a KS3 and 4 Pupil Referral Unit that caters for secondary aged pupils who are permanently excluded, on respite from their home schools, Year 11 pupils without a school place and new arrivals into the borough.
It caters for both boys and girls.
Most students at Canterbury Campus have had difficulties in mainstream settings and will have been excluded or have been referred for a period of timed intervention, assessment and/or behavioural support and other types of intervention. After assessment, some students may require an Education, Health and Care Plan.
Many pupils have Social and Emotional difficulties and some have associated learning difficulties which are wide ranging in terms of severity.
We work closely with a range of professionals, with our own Safer Schools Officer on site twice a week, a Speech and Language therapist, Educational Psychologist and CAMHS worker.
Each student has an Individual Learning Plan that includes social development opportunities. Students are taught in small groups and take a wide range of GCSE subjects in Year 10 and Year 11. Our aim is for students to reintegrate into schools or at the end of Year 11 to move on to Sixth Forms or College.
For more information about Canterbury Campus contact Neil Morris at: nmorris@melbury.merton.sch.uk
Neil Morris Canterbury Campus Headteacher
Canterbury/Lavender Campus Ofsted 2024
Melrose/Whatley Ofsted 2024

pageCache.pageTitle: Melbury College - Melbury College Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Vision
At Melbury College, we are committed to educating the whole child through a personalised, inclusive and trauma-informed approach that promotes wellbeing, belonging and high-quality learning. We believe that positive relationships, built on our shared values of Respect, Courage, Determination, Kindness and Purpose, provide the foundation for every young person to thrive.
Our vision is to create a safe, nurturing and ambitious learning community where every pupil is empowered to overcome barriers, achieve their potential and prepare for successful adult lives. Through a broad, balanced and engaging curriculum, high expectations and personalised support, we develop confident, determined and purposeful learners who are equipped to contribute positively to their communities.
Our Values
At Melbury College, we believe that learning flourishes when young people feel safe, connected, respected and understood. Our values underpin every interaction, every decision and every learning experience. They reflect our commitment to a trauma-informed culture where positive relationships are at the heart of learning, individual strengths are recognised, and every member of our community is supported to grow, achieve and thrive.
By living these values every day, we develop confident, capable and compassionate young people who are prepared to contribute positively to society and pursue their aspirations with courage, determination and purpose.
Canterbury/Lavender Campus Ofsted 2024
Melrose/Whatley Ofsted 2024

pageCache.pageTitle: Melbury College - Welcome from the Head of Melrose School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from Headteacher
Melrose School is a specialist school catering for pupils aged 5-16 years with an Education, Health and Care Plan. All of our pupils have a primary social, emotional, mental health need and many will have additional needs such as ADHD, speech, language and communication needs or experienced current or historical trauma.
All of the children who attend Melrose School do so because mainstream education was not able to meet their needs and therefore our primary aim is to provide a nurturing and safe environment to re-engage children in their learning.
All pupils benefit from small class sizes and teaching from a highly skilled and nurturing staff team. Pupils in Primary are taught across four mixed-aged classes. Pupils in Years 7-9 are taught in what we refer to as our ‘Nurture Provision’ which is an extension of our Primary teaching model offering extended support for pupils who would benefit from one classroom base with consistent teaching staff for the majority of the school day. Pupils in Key Stages 1-3 access the range of National Curriculum subjects which are differentiated and presented in creative and meaningful ways.
Key Stage 4 pupils continue to be taught in small class sizes whilst having access to pastoral support from an assigned Tutor and subjects being taught by specialist teachers. Pupils work towards GCSE or equivalent qualifications which are bespoke to each pupils’ needs and enables pupils to move on to their next educational pathway. We also work closely with alternative education providers to offer a range of vocational courses providing further qualification options based on pupils’ needs and interests.
Our curriculum provision is enhanced through weekly sessions known as Social Development Opportunities that offer the pupils experiences that develop their self-esteem and resilience such as cooking, rock climbing and sports coaching.
We work with a range of professionals who are integrated within the life of Melrose school and offer pupils access to specialist services and therapeutic provision. This includes CAMHS, Art and Play Therapists, Speech and Language Therapists, Occupational Therapists, Educational Psychologists, Safer Schools Officer, Social Worker and Greenhouse Mentor.
We are very proud of the provision we offer our pupils and would be pleased to welcome you in our school to learn more.
For more information about Melrose School, please contact Amanda Addy at: aaddy@melbury.merton.sch.uk
Canterbury/Lavender Campus Ofsted 2024
Melrose/Whatley Ofsted 2024

pageCache.pageTitle: Melbury College - Welcome from the Headteacher
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
At Lavender Campus, we offer high quality, bespoke education provision for students of compulsory school age (5-16), who live in Merton and who are too unwell to attend their home school because of medical and/or mental health needs
My name is Jessica Husaini, the Head of Lavender provision. Welcome to our site where I hope you will be able to find the answers to the questions you may have.
If a child is unable to attend school because of a mental or medical health condition, we can provide bespoke and ambitious on going learning until they are well enough to reintegrate back into school or college.
We offer a variety of services:
We hold high expectations for all of our students, in all spheres of education and engagement. In Lavender our students concentrate on GCSE, / Functional Skills exams, and AQA awards in core subjects alongside a well-established programme of well-being and extra-curricular activity. Our outreach teaching follows the home school’s curriculum where the frequency of tuition will be appropriate to however much the student’s condition allows.
We offer an enhanced PSHE and well being curriculum, with an onus on building resilience and self-esteem. Throughout a young person’s stay at Lavender, we consider the next academic steps: either back into mainstream, special education or a post 16 placement. We provide careers and academic pathway information on an individual basis to enable our students to continue to flourish post Lavender.
We work closely with other services to deliver a supportive curriculum, eg: CAMHS, Tangled Feet, offering Art, Drama and Music Therapy, Speech and Language Therapy, Educational Psychology, Occupational Therapy, Education Welfare and My Futures.
We are based in Mitcham at Tamworth recreation ground. Our students have access to specialist classrooms, a Yoga studio, outside space and a dining/common room. They have the opportunity to work out on our outdoor gym equipment, play table tennis and table football, badminton, or simply enjoy our developing sensory garden.
Our students are supported in small classes, with a dedicated and specialist staff team. We strive to offer a calm, safe and nurturing environment where we enable our young people to flourish.
For more information on Lavender Campus contact us at: lavenderoffice@melbury.merton.sch.uk
For more information on supporting children with medical needs, please refer to: Supporting Pupils at School with Medical Conditions and Education for Children with Health Needs who Cannot Attend School
A few words from Gina, Lavender’s CAMHS psychologist: Why Activity and Routine Strengthen Wellbeing
Head of Lavender Campus

pageCache.pageTitle: Melbury College - Welcome from the Exec Head
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Building Relationships. Inspiring Resilience. Unlocking Potential
As a partnership of specialist education provisions serving the London Borough of Merton, we support children and young people with Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) needs, medical needs and those requiring alternative educational pathways. We are proud to provide personalised, inclusive and ambitious education that places wellbeing, belonging and achievement at the heart of everything we do.
Our vision is to educate the whole child through a personalised, inclusive and trauma-informed approach that promotes wellbeing, belonging and high-quality learning. We recognise that positive relationships provide the foundation for engagement, resilience and success, and we create the conditions in which every young person can feel safe, connect with others, engage in learning and achieve.
Building Relationships
Relationships are at the heart of our ethos. We know that young people learn best when they feel connected, understood and respected. Through trusting, respectful and consistent relationships, we create calm, nurturing and predictable environments where pupils can develop confidence, emotional wellbeing and a genuine sense of belonging.
Our value of Respect means valuing every person and celebrating diversity. Kindness encourages us to show compassion, empathy and care for others. Together, these values help create a community where everyone feels heard, valued and included.
Inspiring Resilience
Our trauma-informed approach reflects our commitment to understanding the whole child. We recognise the impact that life experiences can have on learning, behaviour and emotional wellbeing, and respond with empathy, consistency and high expectations.
Our values of Courage and Determination encourage young people to embrace challenge, make positive choices, persevere when things become difficult and continue striving towards their goals. We want our pupils to develop the emotional regulation, confidence and learning stamina they need to respond positively to setbacks and grow from their experiences.
We are ambitious for every learner. Through a broad, balanced and engaging curriculum, we develop knowledge alongside confidence, independence, character and life skills. We maintain high expectations while providing personalised pathways and specialist support that remove barriers to learning and enable every young person to succeed.
Our value of Purpose encourages pupils to aim high, take responsibility and recognise the positive difference they can make. We want every young person to leave Melbury with a sense of direction, possibility and belief in what they can achieve.
Our values of Respect, Courage, Determination, Kindness and Purpose are more than words on a page. They shape our culture, guide our decisions and influence every interaction across our college community. They provide a shared language for how we learn, lead and work together, helping us to create a community where young people are encouraged to grow, achieve and aspire.
We know that the greatest impact is achieved through partnership. By working closely with families, schools, health professionals and the wider community, we provide the holistic support that each young person needs to flourish. Together, we help our pupils develop the knowledge, skills, confidence and character they need to thrive in education, employment and life.
I am incredibly proud of our dedicated staff, whose expertise, compassion and unwavering commitment make Melbury College such a special place to learn and grow. Every day, they make a lasting difference to the lives of our pupils and their families, helping young people recognise their strengths, overcome challenges and discover what they are capable of achieving.
Whether you are a parent, carer, professional, prospective colleague or visitor, I hope our website gives you a genuine sense of who we are and what we stand for. We look forward to welcoming you to Melbury College and working alongside you to Build Relationships, Inspire Resilience and Unlock Potential for every child and young person in our care.
Carla Chandler (Executive Head Teacher)
Canterbury/Lavender Campus Ofsted 2024
Melrose/Whatley Ofsted 2024

pageCache.pageTitle: Melbury College - Welcome from the Alternative Education Headteacher
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Alternative Education Headteacher
Cobham Court is a provision that operates within Melbury College and as such is linked to both The Canterbury Campus and Melrose School.
Worsfold House/Cobham Court is a specialist provision which creates bespoke educational packages for a wide variety of pupils with a wide range of needs. We work with local authorities to cater for students with EHCP’s at our Worsfold House site, as well as offering respite and timed interventions for students across Melbury College at our Cobham Court site.
On being admitted to our sites students are allocated a key worker to support them both personally and academically. Students at Worsfold House follow a curriculum, which is similar to that offered at Melrose school and for afternoon lessons we use their staff and facilities. Students at Cobham Court follow a core curriculum. All students, regardless of their pathway study English, Maths and Science and the Princes Trust award.
Students have access to a range of facilities including a gym, indoor recreation areas and cooking facilities. Cobham Court also arranges and oversees alternative provision placements for students within a continuous monitoring framework. We are currently in partnership with Tooting and Mitcham FC and also offer in house vocational activities including Barbering and Hair and Beauty. In the Summer term 2023 we will be launching an offsite motor mechanics Course
For more information about the Cobham Court contact Nigel Hill, Alternative Provision Headteacher at: alternativeprovision@melbury.merton.sch.uk
Alternative Education Headteacher

Melrose/Whatley Ofsted 2024

pageCache.pageTitle: Melbury College - Welcome from the Head of Whatley Campus
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Head
We offer a bespoke education tailored to each student’s individual strengths and needs within a calm and supportive setting. Our therapeutic and academic curriculum is rooted in neurodiversity-affirming practice, valuing every student’s individuality while helping them develop the skills they need for life beyond school. We support young people to grow in confidence, independence and resilience as they prepare for adulthood, including developing an understanding of future career pathways, gaining practical life skills and accessing opportunities that help them build experience of the wider world.
All students benefit from small class sizes and a high adult-to-student ratio. Our highly trained teachers and teaching assistants work alongside on-site therapeutic professionals as part of a dedicated and nurturing staff team.
We provide a range of curriculum pathways, ensuring that student wellbeing, engagement and progress remain at the heart of everything we do.
We are extremely proud of our students, our staff and our wider school community, and we warmly invite you to visit Whatley Campus to experience our school for yourself.
For more information about Whatley Campus, please contact:

pageCache.pageTitle: Melbury College - Welcome from Melrose Primary
pageCache.text:
Welcome from Melrose Primary
Melrose Primary is a specialist school catering for up to 24 pupils with an Education, Health and Care Plan.
All of our children have a primary social, emotional, mental health need and many will have additional needs such as ADHD, speech, language and communication needs or experienced current or historical trauma. All of the children who attend Melrose Primary do so because their mainstream setting was not able to meet their needs and therefore our primary aim is to provide a nurturing and safe environment to re-engage children in their learning.
At Melrose Primary, we offer the full range of National Curriculum subjects differentiated and presented in a meaningful and creative way. Our focus is on developing children’s literacy and language skills as well as their personal and social development skills. Our curriculum provision is enhanced through weekly sessions known as Social Development Opportunities that offer the children experiences that develop their self-esteem and resilience such as cooking, farm workshops and sports coaching.
We also offer 5 Melrose Primary Assessment Placements for primary aged pupils who are undergoing a statutory assessment for EHCP and who are struggling within their current mainstream provision. Places are allocated via Merton SEN panel following a referral from Merton’s Virtual Behaviour Service (VBS). Pupils who attend on an assessment place are offered a short-term provision and are fully integrated into the life of the school. Pupils remain with us until a suitable long-term placement has been found.
Children have access to a wider range of professionals including CAMHS, Speech and Language therapists and Play therapists and are supported by a highly skilled and nurturing staff team. If you are interested in learning more about our school please contact Amanda on 020 8646 2620 and we would be happy to welcome you to our school.
Please watch our short video to see how we are supporting our families at Melrose Primary School
Headteacher - Primary
Canterbury/Lavender Campus Ofsted 2024
Melrose/Whatley Ofsted 2024

Careers
At Melrose School, we are committed to ensuring that all our students in years 7 to 11 have high quality impartial advice on career opportunities, and that they progress onto appropriate courses or employment on leaving the school. It is very important to us to know that all leavers have a plan for their next step.
“Our mission is to inspire all our students to make the best transition possible into the right choice for their next steps, whether that is employment, further or higher education, and to support in the development of the skills needed to manage a fulfilling career in a changing world.”
We support our students in making well-informed decisions by providing access to differentiated, impartial and independent information and guidance about the range of options (including academic, vocational, apprenticeships) that are most likely to help them to achieve their ambitions. We believe that giving students the best careers education and guidance is vital to improving their motivation to learn and help them to achieve.
Your designated Careers Lead at Melrose School is Carlie Holliday. You can contact Carlie via email at cholliday@melbury.merton.sch.uk or via telephone 020 8646 2620.
Advice for Employers and Partners
We would like to engage with employers both locally and nationally, in order to give our students the best opportunity to understand the world of work and understand the importance of developing their own skills and aptitudes to support them as they progress through Melrose.
We are still building strong links with a wide number of different employers who have been supportive of the work, which we are doing with our students.
We would love to engage more employers in the work, which we have been doing. If you would like to be involved in any of the events which we plan to run, or feel that you would be able to contribute to our Careers Programme in any way, please contact our Careers Lead, Carlie Holliday.
Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) is delivered through a range of activities for every student from Year 7 to Year 11. During a planned programme which gives students the opportunity to examine a wide range of future careers options, learning about pathways, careers roles and Labour Market Information. Students also have the opportunity to develop their employability skills, encounter providers of further and higher education and learn from employers. The CEIAG programme is designed to help the Academy work towards the Gatsby Benchmarks and satisfy the statutory guidelines outlined in DFE guidance.
Work Experience Placements
We pride ourselves on finding appropriate Work Experience Placements for our Year 10 pupils in the Summer Term. This is a two-week block that provides them with a solid experience in the work place environment.
Our placements to date have included: local primary schools, panel beating centres, Go karting tracks, school kitchens and caretaker support roles.
If you feel that you could support us in building connections with work experience placements, please do contact Carlie Holliday.
